ai.description: This 10–12 cm lizard is grey-brown with dark crossbands and a pale vertebral stripe. It features a flattened body, spiny scales, and exceptionally long, curved claws on the hind feet.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Trapelus megalonyx* is distinguished by its exceptionally long, curved claws and a lack of the distinct, enlarged spiny scales typically found on the flanks of other agamas.
ai.habitat: The Afghan Ground Agama inhabits arid, rocky, or sandy desert landscapes with sparse xerophytic vegetation, typically found at elevations ranging from 500 to 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Afghan Ground Agama is a diurnal lizard that frequently exhibits a defensive "push-up" display, bobbing its body to signal territory or warn off potential threats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Trapelus megalonyx* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–8 eggs. Breeding occurs during the spring and early summer months.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Trapelus megalonyx* is found in the arid regions of Pakistan and northwestern India (Rajasthan), typically inhabiting sandy or rocky deserts at low to moderate elevations.
